round: CodeRabbit round 1 on PR #109 (8 findings: 6 Minor + 2 Major); R1-R5/F1-F3 design NOT redone

Major-7.what: the post-write read-back in `bindReseededSeat` must ROLL BACK a write that landed when it throws or answers another handle, must not overwrite a concurrent writer's newer document, and must report a rollback that did not restore
landing: packages/mpd-cellwork-plugin/src/protocol-core.ts#promoteAfterHandoff — carries the rollback on the refusal

implementation.restore: the SNAPSHOT's seat row (`previousSeat`: executorRef AND mode, handoff kept) and the SNAPSHOT's board field (`previousTasks`, restored wholesale) are written back; the CELL row is the barrier's and is written later from the refusal outcome, so it keeps the old session and is fenced
implementation.no-overwrite: the rollback re-reads the file and rewrites ONLY when its bytes are EXACTLY `writtenText`; any difference answers `rollback:"refused"` and the reason sentence contains the literal `rollback refused due to concurrent change` — the other writer's document is left untouched
implementation.failure-is-loud: a rollback whose re-read or write fails answers `rollback:"failed"` with the sentence and `rollbackReason`; the bind's `reason` (which carries that sentence) is the `checkpoint-unrecoverable.reason` and the two rollback fields land on the same journal row
implementation.throw-and-mismatch: the read-back is wrapped in try/catch; a throw is classified `surface:"team-record-verify"` (the sentence keeps `after the child started`, so the existing A5 throw arm still measures it), a non-throwing wrong handle is `surface:"team-member"` — BOTH go through `rollbackBind`

arms: A5 (second arm, extended): a read-back that THROWS rolls back — journal `rollback:"restored"`, TEAM `executorRef` and board `T1.owner` both back to the OLD handle
A11: a STALE non-throwing read-back rolls back — seat row `executorRef`/`mode`/handoff and `T1.owner`/revision restored, cell row keeps the old session and is fenced

A12: a concurrent write at the read-back makes the rollback refuse — `rollback:"refused"`, the other writer's document (`phase:"concurrent-writer"`, old/old pair) is byte-preserved, and the captain's `cellwork_dispatch {unfence:["Senior Engineer"]}` clears the fence (recoverable)

The fail-before log proves the FINAL arms red on the HEAD sources and the post log proves them green on the fixed sources; it is not a per-arm revert/restore cycle (one revert covered all seven red arms).

A12's recoverability assertion drives the REAL `cellwork_dispatch {unfence}` tool over a fake plane (`mpdTeamActions.unfence` + a no-op `dispatch`), so it proves the tool-level lever, not a live team-core write.

The rollback concurrency check is exact-byte identity against the bytes this bind wrote. A writer whose document happens to be byte-identical to ours is indistinguishable — that is the CAS's inherent bound, not a new one.

Major-8 removed the branch's FENCE entirely (the record is unreadable, so no merge base exists). Contract §3 A5's phrase 'fences the seat' is therefore reconciled as: journaled always, fenced only when a trustworthy write exists — the task's Major-8 explicitly requires `not persisted` over a claimed fence.
No `unfenceSeats`/`adoptSeat` read-failure fallback (pre-existing: an unreadable record falls back to the pre-await snapshot) was changed; that code is outside the 8 findings.
The dist stamp was built from the same source hashes recorded in sha256.txt; `verify-dist-fresh` re-derives them, so the committed dist is proven fresh, not merely rebuilt.
